title: Schematic density in fibres spreads from the generic fibre
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose $Y$ is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components] with generic point $\eta$ [def-sc-generic-point]. Let $U\subseteq X$ be any open subscheme. For $y\in Y$ put $X_y=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ and $U_y=U\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-weil-residue-field]. If $j_\eta:U_\eta\hookrightarrow X_\eta$ induces an injective map of sheaves $\mathcal O_{X_\eta}\to(j_\eta)_*\mathcal O_{U_\eta}$, then there is a nonempty open subset $V\subseteq Y$ such that for every $y\in V$, the inclusion $j_y:U_y\hookrightarrow X_y$ induces an injective map $\mathcal O_{X_y}\to(j_y)_*\mathcal O_{U_y}$. This injectivity is the meaning of scheme-theoretic density here; neither $U\to X$ nor $f$ is assumed quasi-separated, and $Y$ need not be reduced or Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 0573, lemma-scheme-theoretically-dense-generic-fibre, statement; schematic-density meaning in morphisms.tex Tag 01RE, lemma-characterize-scheme-theoretically-dense

proof.text: Replace $Y$ by its reduction and $X,U$ by their base changes. By the definition of reduction, on an affine chart this replaces $A$ by $A/\sqrt{0}$. Every map $A\to\kappa(y)$ kills $\sqrt{0}$, and the local quotient $(A/\sqrt{0})_{\mathfrak p/\sqrt{0}}$ has residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Thus the point sets, residue fields, and fibre products defining $X_y,U_y$ are unchanged. Finite type survives this base change. The reduced irreducible base is integral by the integral-scheme characterization. Restrict to a nonempty affine open of it, obtaining $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A$ a domain and fraction field $K$. The open eventually found here is also an open of the original base.

source.place: Tag 0573, proof, first paragraph; reduction quotient calculation written out

proof.text: Finite type over affine $Y$ gives a finite affine cover $X=\bigcup_{r=1}^N X_r$ with each $X_r=\operatorname{Spec}B_r$ finite type over $A$. The sheaf injection on the generic fibre restricts to each $(X_r)_\eta$; after proving the result on each chart, intersect the finitely many base opens. Fix one chart and write $B=B_r$. Its generic fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A K)$. A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and $K$, so finite-type permanence makes $B_K$ Noetherian. Its spectrum is Noetherian and every subset, in particular $U_\eta\cap(X_r)_\eta$, is quasi-compact. Cover $U\cap X_r$ by principal opens $D(g)\subseteq U\cap X_r$ using the principal-open basis on $\operatorname{Spec}B$. Their inverse images cover $U_\eta\cap(X_r)_\eta$; quasi-compactness chooses finitely many $g_1,\ldots,g_m\in B$. Hence $D(g_i)\subseteq U\cap X_r$ holds on the total chart, and their generic fibres cover its $U_\eta$.

source.place: Tag 0573, proof, second and third paragraphs

proof.text: Apply the affine density criterion on the generic fibre. It gives injectivity of $\mu_K:B_K\to B_K^{\oplus m}$, $b\mapsto(g_1b,\ldots,g_mb)$. Define $\mu:B\to B^{\oplus m}$ by the same formula and $M=\operatorname{coker}\mu$. The images of the $m$ standard basis vectors generate $M$ as a $B$-module, including $M=0$ when $m=0$.

source.place: Tag 0573, proof, third paragraph; Algebra Tag 0565 and Morphisms Tags 056C, 01RE

proof.text: Obtain the simultaneous flatness needed in Tag 0573 from the existing algebra generic-flatness tool as follows. Form the square-zero algebra $E=B\oplus M$ with $(b,u)(c,v)=(bc,bv+cu)$ and unit $(1,0)$; associativity follows by expanding each side to $(bcd,bcw+bdv+cdu)$. If $b_j$ generate $B$ over $A$ and $u_i$ generate $M$ over $B$, then $(b_j,0)$ and $(0,u_i)$ generate $E$ over $A$: products with $(b,0)$ give every $(0,bu_i)$. Apply algebra generic flatness to $A\to E$, obtaining nonzero $a\in A$ with $E_a$ flat over $A$. Fractions identify $E_a=B_a\oplus M_a$ as $A$-modules. For any injection $P\to Q$, its tensor with $E_a$ is injective by flatness; the maps on the two summands are therefore injective separately. By the definition of flatness, both $B_a$ and $M_a$ are flat over $A$. All subsequent arguments are on $D(a)$, where tensoring with $\kappa(y)$ or $K$ is unchanged by this localization. No finite-presentation conclusion is needed.

source.place: Tag 0573, generic-flatness paragraph; agent-written square-zero specialization of the algebra case of Tag 051T

proof.text: The localized map $\mu_a:B_a\to B_a^{\oplus m}$ is injective. Indeed, for nonzero $s\in A$, multiplication by $s$ on $A$ is injective; tensor with the flat $A$-module $B_a$ to see that multiplication by $s$ on $B_a$ is injective. Thus $B_a$ is torsion-free. The map $B_a\to B_K$ is injective: a fraction mapping to zero is killed by a nonzero base scalar, and hence is zero. If $b\in\ker\mu_a$, its image in $B_K$ lies in $\ker\mu_K=0$, so $b=0$. Fractions also identify $\operatorname{coker}\mu_a=M_a$: every localized cokernel class lifts from a fraction in $B^{\oplus m}$, and a class is zero precisely when a power of $a$ puts its numerator in $\operatorname{im}\mu$. Consequently $0\to B_a\xrightarrow{\mu_a}B_a^{\oplus m}\to M_a\to0$ is exact.

source.place: Tag 0573, fourth paragraph; flat-implies-torsion-free argument and localization exactness written out

proof.text: For $y\in D(a)$ tensor this short exact sequence over $A$ with $\kappa(y)$. The flat-quotient tensor theorem applies because $M_a$ is flat over $A$. It makes the map $B\otimes_A\kappa(y)\to(B\otimes_A\kappa(y))^{\oplus m}$, $b\mapsto((g_i\otimes1)b)_i$, injective. The affine criterion says that $W_y=\bigcup_i D(g_i\otimes1)$ has injective structure-sheaf restriction from $X_y$. Since the total-space opens $D(g_i)$ were chosen inside $U$, we have $W_y\subseteq U_y$. A section on any open of $X_y$ vanishing on its intersection with $U_y$ vanishes on its intersection with $W_y$, and hence is zero. This proves the required sheaf injection for the chart.

For each chart take the resulting nonempty base open, and intersect all finitely many of them. This intersection contains the generic point: every nonempty open of an irreducible scheme contains its generic point. Thus it is nonempty. For a fibre over this intersection, the chart fibres cover $X_y$. A section in the kernel of $\mathcal O_{X_y}\to(j_y)_*\mathcal O_{U_y}$ restricts to zero on every chart by the previous step, and is zero by the sheaf axiom. The same applies on every open of $X_y$, giving the claimed sheaf injection. If there are no charts, $X$ is empty and any nonempty affine base open works.

source.place: Tag 0573, affine-cover reduction and final conclusion

The item statement is byte-identical to an earlier unsplit copy and matches 0573, with density written as O→j_*O_U injective per 01RE; no hypothesis was added. The 7 steps follow 0573 and each cited statement says what is used. (1) Reduction keeps the points and residue fields, so the fibres are the same; the reduced irreducible base is integral; restrict to a domain chart. (2) Use the finite affine cover from the finite-type definition; B_K is Noetherian, so U_η∩(X_r)_η is quasi-compact; the principal opens D(g)⊆U∩X_r are chosen on the total chart. (3) The new criterion gives injectivity of μ_K. (4) Apply the generic-flatness tool (domain, finite type, no fp) to the square-zero algebra E=B⊕M; E_a is flat over A, so its summands B_a and M_a are flat; this is a valid replacement for the 051T use. (5) Torsion-freeness gives B_a⊂B_K, so ker μ_a=0 and coker μ_a=M_a by fractions. (6) The flat-quotient tensor lemma with N=κ(y) and the criterion give W_y⊆U_y, and density passes from W_y to U_y by testing sections. (7) Intersect the finitely many D(a_r), which contain η, and glue by the sheaf axiom. New node lem-trf-affine-schematic-density-criterion is true; I tested n=0, n=1, k[x]/(x²) and k[x,y]/(xy) and checked the sheaf clause directly. It is statement-only, self-contained and smaller than the item. The DAG grep for 0565/01RE/056C/0573 and for density keywords found no duplicate (the Nagata qc-only definition and the topological lem-sbc-generic-open-fibre-density are different statements).
